To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most appropriate method for measuring the outcomes of rehabilitation is the individual rehabilitation plan.

(1) there is no one best outcome measure; (2) there are a variety of measures that can be used to assess the effectiveness of a program; and (3) the most appropriate measure for a particular program is the one that is most closely aligned with the goals of that program.
the use of individualized goals and outcomes in rehabilitation is valid and reliable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how we can best measure the outcome of rehabilitation services. The answer we propose is that we should be measuring the outcomes of the services we provide for individuals.
the development of a method for measuring outcomes of rehabilitation services that is both individually determined and institutionally applicable.

developing and validating a method for determining the outcome of individual rehabilitation services that is both meaningful to the purchaser and applicable to the needs and expectations of the service provider and the client.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
individually determined outcomes should be the basis for measuring rehabilitation services and the outcomes of rehabilitation services.

the most effective way to measure the outcome of a rehabilitation program is by the use of a standardized instrument that is individually administered to the client and that measures the specific outcomes that were individually determined as being relevant to the client's needs.
individually determined outcome measures are valid and reliable measures of rehabilitation services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the individualized outcome measures that are used to evaluate rehabilitation services are more appropriate than standardized outcome measures in evaluating the effectiveness of rehabilitation services.
the use of individually determined outcome measures in rehabilitation will provide purchasers with a more accurate measure of the value received for the funds expended.
the individualized goals of our clients are the most valid measure for determining outcomes of rehabilitation service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the purchaser of rehabilitation services must have a clear understanding of the outcomes they wish to measure.
there is no reason that we should be forced to abandon our individualized approach to service delivery in order to meet the needs of our purchasers.
the outcomes we are seeking in rehabilitation are best measured by those who have a vested interest in the outcome, the individual and their family.
